summary.title: Activation of Macrophages by CpG DNA and LPS: an FTIR Spectroscopic Study
summary.authors: Emrulla Spahiu; Senol Dogan; Jörg Schnauß; Mayda Gursel; Feride Severcan
summary.executive_summary: This study investigates the global molecular changes in murine macrophage RAW 264.7 cells upon activation with CpG DNA and lipopolysaccharide (LPS) using Attenuated Total Reflectance Fourier Transform Infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy. The researchers aimed to determine if these immune activators induce detectable spectral shifts indicative of specific metabolic pathways. Using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), the study identified that CpG DNA and LPS treatments significantly increase total nucleic acid concentrations starting from early time points post-activation. Specifically, DNA synthesis follows RNA synthesis, with RNA-specific peaks indicating the activation state within the first minutes of treatment. Both stimuli cause an initial rapid increase in total protein concentration that levels off by two hours. Furthermore, both groups show increased concentrations of fatty acids, triglycerides, and cholesterol, suggesting a shared synthesis pathway and de novo lipogenesis. The study concludes that FTIR spectroscopy serves as an independent modality to monitor macrophage activation dynamics, offering a non-destructive, high-throughput alternative to complex omics techniques that require extensive sample preparation. The findings provide a broad view of relative metabolite amounts, including nucleic acids, lipids, and proteins, which are not readily accessible by other methods.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This study investigates the global molecular changes in murine macrophage RAW 264.7 cells upon activation with CpG DNA and lipopolysaccharide (LPS) using Attenuated Total Reflectance Fourier Transform Infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy. The researchers aimed to determine if these immune activators induce detectable spectral shifts indicative of specific metabolic pathways. Using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), the study identified that CpG DNA and LPS treatments significantly increase total nucleic acid concentrations starting from early time points post-activation. Specifically, DNA synthesis follows RNA synthesis, with RNA-specific peaks indicating the activation state within the first minutes of treatment. Both stimuli cause an initial rapid increase in total protein concentration that levels off by two hours. Furthermore, both groups show increased concentrations of fatty acids, triglycerides, and cholesterol, suggesting a shared synthesis pathway and de novo lipogenesis. The study concludes that FTIR spectroscopy serves as an independent modality to monitor macrophage activation dynamics, offering a non-destructive, high-throughput alternative to complex omics techniques that require extensive sample preparation. The findings provide a broad view of relative metabolite amounts, including nucleic acids, lipids, and proteins, which are not readily accessible by other methods.

Research Context
FTIR spectroscopy allows non-destructive, rapid, and high-throughput analysis of biological systems. The absorbance of IR light by water molecules is a limitation of infrared spectroscopy. ATR unit offers a handy use of spectrometer since the sample is directly put onto the ATR crystal. Macrophage cells constitute the front line of the immune system defending the organism against invaders. CpG DNA triggers the proliferation of macrophages, the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines. Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) is one of the main constituents of the cell wall of gram-negative bacteria. How CpG ODN-mediated immune activation impacts relative amounts of nucleic acids, lipids, proteins, and other metabolites has not been studied. Even though the trending omics techniques yield precise quantitative data on specific molecules rather than the bulk analysis done by FTIR spectroscopy. The simple, rapid, and non-invasive experimental setup using bulk FTIR analysis proves to give a broad view.

Research Question And Hypothesis
Whether CpG ODN-mediated immune activation leads to global molecular changes in cells that are detectable by FTIR spectroscopy is currently unknown. The study uses ATR-FTIR spectroscopy to monitor the molecular changes in murine macrophage RAW 264.7 cells upon activation with CpG DNA and LPS. By PCA analysis, we identified the sources of variation to follow with detailed spectral analysis. CpG DNA and LPS treatment increase the total nucleic acid concentration from the early periods post-activation. DNA synthesis follows RNA synthesis. RNA-specific peak shows the activation state of macrophages in early periods post-treatment. CpG DNA and LPS result in an initial rapid increase in the total protein concentration, leveling off two hours post-activation. Both activated groups increase the concentration of fatty acids, triglycerides, and cholesterol, pointing out to a shared synthesis pathway. This study, for the first time, demonstrates the use of FTIR spectroscopy as an independent modality to monitor the activation dynamics.

Methodological Details
Murine macrophage-like RAW 264.7 cells were cultured at 37 °C with 5% CO 2 in Dulbecco's modified Eagle's medium. The medium was supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 2 mM L-glutamine. Cells were harvested, spun at 1000 rpm 208 g for 10 min, and resuspended at a concentration of 2x10 6 /mL. Control group was treated with phosphate-buffered saline (0.9% PBS; Sigma, USA). CpG DNA stimulated group was treated with 1 µM K3 ODN (Endotoxin-free; Integrated DNA Technologies, Belgium). LPS stimulated group was treated with 0.5 µg/ml LPS (Sigma, USA). Four different times points following treatment were used for measurements to evaluate the kinetics of induced effects: 10 min, 30 min, 2 h, and 6 h. All infrared interferograms were collected using a Perkin-Elmer Spectrum One FTIR spectrometer with the ATR unit (Diamond-ZnSe crystal) attached. The spectra of cell samples were recorded in the 4000-650 cm -1 region at 25°C. Cell samples of 1 µl were dried with mild N 2 flux for 5 min. The best signal-to-noise ratio for interferogram collection was achieved with a 128 scan number and 2 cm -1 spectral resolution. Replicates (n=5) were used in data analysis. Post-processing of the spectral data included 13-point Savitzky-Golay smoothing and baseline correction. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was performed using the spectra imported directly into the Unscrambler 11.0 software. Shapiro-Wilk and Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests were used to determine the normality of our datasets with the GraphPad Prism 8.

Procedures And Architectures
The study used Attenuated Total Reflectance (ATR) Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy to monitor molecular changes. By PCA analysis, we identified the sources of variation to follow with detailed spectral analysis. Principal Component (PC)-1 gave a variability of 83% and provided information for the vast source of variation. PC-2, which had a variability of 11%. The patterns observed in the Scores Plot show a considerable amount of samples being clustered according to the treatment. The peaks related to nucleic acids-phosphate vibration (1238 cm -1 ), and symmetric PO -2 stretching (1085 cm -1 )-show prominent differences. The peak integration values (corresponding to concentration) are shown as bar diagrams in Figure 2 .B. Stimulation with CpG DNA has significantly increased this peak value from the first minutes (p < 0.001***). This increase is maintained until 2 h after stimulation (p < 0.1*). Amide I (1639 cm -1 ) and amide II (1540 cm -1 ) peaks are used for protein content analysis. There is a significant increase in the total protein content of CpG DNA treated cells from 10 min post-treatment until 2 h. There was a very significant increase in the peak during activation correlating to an increased concentration of triglycerides and cholesterol. A significant increase is observed in fatty acid concentration as well, pointing out to the previously documented de novo lipogenesis. The second derivative spectrum was used for the side-peak band assignment. Concentration studies were carried out by integrating the curves under the peaks.

Key Results
CpG DNA stimulation induced significant changes in nucleic acid content (1238 cm -1 peak integration) of macrophages starting from 10 min until 6 h after treatment (p < 0.1*). Stimulation with CpG DNA has significantly increased this peak value from the first minutes (p < 0.001***). This increase is maintained until 2 h after stimulation (p < 0.1*). The time until 2 h after stimulation seems to be the period of extensive RNA synthesis. DNA synthesis starts from 6 h after stimulation with CpG DNA. LPS, on the other hand, has an increased concentration of total RNA up to 2 h post-stimulation. There is a significant increase in the total protein content of CpG DNA treated cells from 10 min post-treatment until 2 h (p < 0.001***). The initial increase in protein concentration is reduced, starting from 2 h time point. There was a very significant increase in the peak during activation correlating to an increased concentration of triglycerides and cholesterol starting from the very first minutes of stimulation. LPS stimulation, on the other hand, elevated the triglycerides and cholesterol concentration after 10 min. A significant increase is observed in fatty acid concentration as well, pointing out to the previously documented de novo lipogenesis. Both activated groups increase the concentration of fatty acids, triglycerides, and cholesterol, pointing out to a shared synthesis pathway. This study, for the first time, demonstrates the use of FTIR spectroscopy as an independent modality to monitor the activation dynamics.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The results of our study deduce that by using the RNA-specific peak (915 cm -1 ), one can define the activation state of macrophages at the very first minutes of activation. All put together, contribution to nucleic acid-related peaks comes from DNA or RNA in a time-dependent manner. The time until 2 h after stimulation seems to be the period of extensive RNA synthesis. This validates the reason for no significant changes occurring in nucleic acid content after 6 h of stimulation. Our work provides an aerial view of the total protein fate and points out to the need for a study of mechanisms in CpG DNA induced protein loss. The lipid metabolism modifications based on the cell activation state can also be investigated in our samples by FTIR spectroscopy. This previously unknown link was elaborated in a recent study on macrophage activation using different TLR agonists. The same study drew attention to the importance of the pathway in cancer cells, where CpG-activated anti-tumor activity of macrophages is essential. The simple, rapid, and non-invasive experimental setup using bulk FTIR analysis proves to give a broad view. The repertoire of genes being repressed covers the ones related to cell cycle, entirely consistent with previous studies.

Our work provides an aerial view of the total protein fate and points out to the need for a study of mechanisms in CpG DNA induced protein loss in the future. The absorbance of IR light by water molecules is a limitation of infrared spectroscopy since it superimposes other signals of the aqueous cell systems. Even though the trending omics techniques yield precise quantitative data on specific molecules rather than the bulk analysis done by FTIR spectroscopy. They require complex sample preparation steps that can result in alterations of chemical ratios and post-translational modifications in lipidomics and proteomics.
